title: Too Much Automation? The Bellwether Effect and Its Implications for Transfer Learning

edges.ref: [7] Burak Turhan, Tim Menzies, Ayse B Bener, Justin Di Stefano. On the relative value of cross-company and within-company data for defect prediction. EMSE 14(5), 2009.
edges.evidence: we compare bellwether against two similarity based transfer learners: the first classic Burak filter from 2009 [7]

edges.target: Turhan initial cross-project result: 60%+ false alarms (Turhan et al.)

edges.evidence: training on S = 9 source projects and testing on T = 1 target projects resulted in alarming high false positive rates (60% or more)

not_reuse_examples: [9] Hall et al. systematic review of fault prediction - cited only as a pointer to background literature, nothing adopted
[14] Lewis et al. Google bug prediction case study - background evidence that defect predictors are 'widely used'; not a premise measurement or method reused
[2] Nam et al. Transfer defect learning (TCA+) - dimensionality-transform method described in §2.2 but explicitly NOT run since paper restricts to homogeneous similarity-based baselines
[34] Krishna et al. 'Which Bad Smells Can Be Ignored' - self pointer for 'more information on this dataset', no reuse
notes: ASE'16 empirical paper (Krishna, Menzies, Fu) proposing bellwether transfer learner; 120 datasets in 4 communities, RF+SMOTE, ED metric, Scott-Knott+bootstrap+A12, Kruskal-Wallis for RQ4; refutes-polarity edges point at Turhan09 Burak filter and Turhan11 which it beats and argues were never necessary; Cohen[50] 'benchmark against simpler' is its closing thesis.
